overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic June Gloom pattern today, with a persistent marine layer producing patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies keeping coastal temperatures suppressed. The running maximum of 64.9°F was reached around 10:52 ET (~7:52 AM PT), and temperatures have stalled with near-zero 30-minute velocity, though the 2-hour trend still shows a modest +0.9°F/hr warming signal. The active NWS alerts (extreme heat, red flag warnings) are all confined to desert and inland areas and have no direct bearing on coastal LA conditions.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster in the 67–70°F range (NBM 67.0, ECMWF 68.4, HRRR 70.2), broadly consistent with the NWS call of 69°F. However, current observed temps are running roughly 4–5°F below the forecast consensus with the marine layer still largely intact. The predicted peak timing from models (~17h ET / ~2 PM PT) suggests meaningful warming potential remains if the fog/cloud deck burns off as expected around midday local time.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a daily high in the 69–71°F range, with the META model's top bucket at 70–71°F (26.5%) and strong secondary probability mass from 72–77°F. The key swing factor is marine layer burn-off timing — a cleaner afternoon clearing could push temps toward 70–71°F (HRRR-leaning), while persistent overcast would cap closer to 67–68°F (NBM-leaning). Confidence is moderate at best; both ensemble bucket sets signal high uncertainty with 'no_trade' abort signals, reflecting the well-known difficulty of forecasting June Gloom clearing depth and timing.
